maria: quick check — running into flaky failures when model func-call returns args that don't match our TS types (eg model returns "3" but schema expects number). Happens more when streaming. Should the JS SDK auto-coerce ("3" -> 3) or fail loudly so consumers handle it?

kenji: i'd vote opt-in coercion. implicit coercion hides mistakes in prompts. we had similar discussion for embeddings earlier. propose adding a small helper + an SDK config flag: `{ toolCall: { coerceOutputs: false } }`.

alex: streaming makes this worse — you often get partial JSON like `{\"count\": 3, \"meta\": {` then next chunk finishes. we should buffer until the model signals done and then attempt a tolerant parse. a small util i use in apps: 

```
function safeExtractJSON(accumulatedStr) {
  // grab last {...} block, naive but works for trailing partials
  const m = accumulatedStr.match(/\{[\s\S]*\}$/);
  if (!m) throw new Error('no JSON payload');
  return JSON.parse(m[0]);
}
```

but we need more robust solution for nested braces and trailing commas.

sophia: +1 on explicit opt-in. i recommend pairing TS generics + runtime validators (zod/joi) so apps get typed outputs and runtime guarantees. example pattern: 

```
const userSchema = z.object({ id: z.number(), name: z.string() })
// after parsing the func-call args (maybe coercing strings->numbers)
const parsed = userSchema.parse(coerceTypes(rawArgs))
```
coerceTypes should be conservative: strings that look like numbers -> number, "true"/"false" -> boolean, iso dates -> Date (opt-in).

maria: good notes. also need to consider python sdk — do we keep behavior parity? probably yes but with pythonic v. types.

bot-build: CI: found failing tests in PR #412 — missing tests for streaming buffer + coercion flag. full log: build/funcall-coerce.test.js:45: expected 2 but got "2"

nina: i'll pick up the tests + add an e2e for streaming partial chunks. plan: add unit tests for `coerceTypes`, integration that simulates chunked model responses, and a docs snippet. assigning to myself, will open branch and ping y'all when ready. @maria @kenji

maria: thanks nina. decision from product side: default `coerceOutputs=false` in SDK, include `coerceTypes` helper in utils package and a `parseStreamedFuncCall` helper that does incremental buffering + final-parse. i'll draft a short RFC/PR with the config shape.

alex: added a small eslint rule locally to catch `FuncCallResult` typed as `any` in our TS tests — will push if it helps.

kenji: :thumbsup: agree. prefer docs + example over magic.

sophia: LGTM — i'll prepare the zod examples for the docs. want to include both `coerceTypes` and `strictParse` variants.

nina: ETA E2E + unit tests by EOD tomorrow, will open PR and add reviewers: @maria @alex @sophia.

maria: perfect. once PR is up i'll mark it for the next maintenance sprint. thanks all :tada:

kenji: quick q — should the helper live in `@redwood-inference/sdk-utils` or `@redwood-inference/sdk` root? my vote utils.

maria: utils is fine. smaller surface area for breaking changes.

alex: also note: add a note in release notes about behavior and migration (if someone relied on implicit coercion before).

sophia: will draft the docs snippet and migration note once PR exists.

bot-build: CI will re-run on the PR branch after tests + lint fixes.

maria: great, closing loop. if anyone hits a hard blocker ping here and i'll escalate.
